story: At 2:17 on this rainy Monday afternoon in Sumter Oaks, Gary is bench-testing his golf cart's light harness and speaker wiring in his garage, keeping everything off the street until it's approved. Out on Magnolia Loop, Donna, Hal, and Rosa are gathered under the lifting shower, and Donna is cheerfully taking Rosa up on a dinner offer, pledging to celebrate at her table if Gary gets through Tuesday without trouble. Hal is pleased that the three flamingos in the yard are a tidy number he can keep track of without any paperwork, and Rosa is happy to see the garage flamingos get a well-earned rest. Everyone seems content, and they're all rooting for Gary.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Bench-build and test the cart's light harness and speaker wiring, keeping it off the street until approved

gary.thought_process: I filed the cart modification request with Architectural Review at tick 369, and L-01 says nothing visible from the street goes on without approval. So I shouldn't bolt the lights onto the exterior yet. But the sound system wiring and the light strings can be bench-built and tested on the workbench in the garage, where nobody can object. It's an afternoon shower, nobody's around, and I'm happiest when my hands are busy. Quiet hours don't apply at 2 PM anyway. Best use of this hour is prepping the lighting harness so it's ready to go the minute approval comes through.

parameters.content: Bench-build and test the cart's light harness and speaker wiring, keeping it off the street until approved

donna.thought_process: Rosa just thanked me for dealing with the flock, and she's offered her kitchen after pickleball. Gary headed home, so he's resting up for Tuesday. I haven't actually answered Rosa yet, and it'd be rude to leave her hanging. A warm, short reply keeps me at the center of the social scene and nudges Rosa toward being part of the Tuesday buzz. Then I can go work on my goal rather than keep chatting.

parameters.content: Rosa, you're a doll, and I'm holding you to that dinner offer. If Gary survives Tuesday without pulling anything, we'll all celebrate at your table.

hal.thought_process: Donna just trimmed the flock to three, so L-02 is satisfied and I've got nothing to report there. I promised myself the notebook stays closed until Monday, and Rosa's table tonight is reward enough for that patience. Rosa thanked Donna and Donna did the right thing without a fuss. A bit of credit is due, said plainly and short. Gary's gone home, so I'll leave him alone and not chase a complaint today.

parameters.content: Three flamingos. That's a number I can count on one hand and not file a thing about. Obliged, Donna.

rosa.thought_process: Hal confirmed Wednesday at nine, so that's settled and I shouldn't ask again. Donna just trimmed the flock down to three, which is exactly what I wanted without a fight. Best move now is to thank her warmly and keep the dinner mood going, then let her get on with her day. I've already said my piece about Tuesday, so this should be a short, genuine acknowledgment of the flock rather than a repeat.

parameters.content: Three flamingos looks lovely from here, Donna, and the garage ones get a well-earned rest. Go enjoy your afternoon, and I'll be rooting for you and Gary on Tuesday.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
